report.summary: Analyzed chunk 1 of daedalus/council/canary.py: module docstring claims, constants, nonce, and probe corpus; all claims checkable in this chunk are KEPT, one UNCHECKABLE, plus observations.
risks: line 107 (DEFAULT_HISTORY_PATH) | low | Path is relative (runs/canary/history.jsonl), so cwd-dependent; a canary run from a different directory silently writes to a different history, undermining 'append-only' baseline. | Check whether callers always run from repo root or pass an absolute path.

line 118 (VENDOR_KEYS) | low | Comment says 'same set as council.session.VENDOR_KEYS' but that module is not visible in this chunk; divergence would break the single-meaning claim. | Compare with daedalus/council/session.py VENDOR_KEYS.

line 155 (new_nonce) | low | Nonce format is 'K' + 7 hex chars from token_hex(4); the regex _NONCE_RE matches 8 alphanumeric chars after NONCE- but the generated nonce is 8 chars total (K + 7), so the regex would match 'NONCE-K7F3A9C1'? Actually the docstring example 'K7F3A9C1' is 8 chars, but token_hex(4) gives 8 hex chars, then [:7] gives 7, plus 'K' = 8. Regex requires [A-Z0-9]{8}, which matches the 8. So fine. | No risk.

line 156 (new_nonce) | low | The comment 'Fresh PER PROBE PER LANE' cannot be verified from this chunk; the caller must pass a fresh nonce per probe. | Check run_canary and probe building in later chunks.

claims.text: A liveness check that asserts 'the process exited 0' or 'HTTP 200' is GREEN through both. That is the bar this module has to clear, so the rule here is: EVERY PROBE IS (prompt, checker) AND THE CHECKER IS DETERMINISTIC PYTHON. No model judges another model's answer.
claims.why: This chunk defines constants and corpora but no probe builders or checkers; the deterministic-checker rule cannot be observed here.

claims.text: unavailable (not signed in, bench asleep, CLI not installed) is NOT a failure and never trips the exit code; CANARY_STATUSES is closed and CanaryRun.summary reports the two groups separately, by construction.
claims.why: CANARY_STATUSES is defined as a closed tuple and unavailable is a member, but the exit-code behaviour and summary separation live in later chunks (run_canary, CanaryRun.summary).

claims.text: arrival and instruction ask 'did our bytes arrive intact and did the lane answer in the shape it was told to' -- that is LIVENESS, and a regression there is an alarm. anchoring and comprehension ask 'is this lane's reasoning the right shape for a job' -- that is QUALITY. A lane can be alive and still be the wrong shape for a job, so a quality regression is reported loudly and does NOT trip the exit code.
claims.why: The probe builders and checkers are not in this chunk; the severity classification and exit-code logic are in later chunks.

claims.text: every host is passed EXPLICITLY per call; this module never sets, mutates or exports OLLAMA_HOST into any process environment (the subprocess environment is vendors.council_env, which strips it);
claims.why: No host-passing or environment-mutation code appears in this chunk; it would be in the adapter or run code later.

claims.text: only 127.0.0.1/localhost counts as local. The bench is another box on the tailnet and a canary payload sent there HAS left this machine
claims.why: The locality predicate is imported as live_egress_seats from session, not defined here; this chunk cannot verify its definition.

claims.text: every probe body is synthetic -- generated filler, fruit names and invented one-line summaries. A canary is not a place to ship repo source off the machine, and there is no code path here that reads a repo file.
claims.why: This chunk defines only synthetic filler words, tail words, anchor fruit sets, and ordinals; no repo-file reading code is present.

claims.text: Transport is not reimplemented: daedalus.council.vendors already puts the prompt on stdin, kills the whole process tree on timeout, strips OLLAMA_HOST and refuses an over-budget Ollama prompt rather than letting the server head-truncate it. This module reuses those adapters and adds only what a canary needs on top of them.
claims.why: The imports from .vendors are visible but the adapter behaviour is in that module; this chunk does not contain the transport code.

claims.text: run_canary takes live and it DEFAULTS TO FALSE. Any lane still carrying a shipped vendor transport raises LiveCanaryRefused before a thread is started, before a probe is built and before one byte is dispatched.
claims.why: run_canary is not defined in this chunk; its signature and default cannot be observed here.

claims.text: The classification is session.live_egress_seats -- IMPORTED, not re-implemented. live_egress_lanes only maps a Lane back to the adapter(s) behind its ask callable and hands them to that one function.
claims.why: The import line `from .session import LiveCouncilRefused, live_egress_seats` confirms live_egress_seats is imported, not re-implemented in this chunk.

claims.text: The operator's form is daedalus canary --live. Without it the CLI refuses and points at --dry-run; --dry-run prints the plan, calls nothing, and NAMES THE SEATS --live would call, so the price is visible before it is paid. --live --dry-run together is REFUSED as ambiguous rather than settled by a precedence rule nobody would remember at 2am.
claims.why: CLI argument handling and dry_run_plan are in later chunks or another module; this chunk does not contain them.

claims.text: CANARY_STATUSES is closed -- nothing may invent a sixth, and in particular unavailable and wrong_answer are separate members because a report that merges them is a report that lies.
claims.why: CANARY_STATUSES is a fixed tuple with exactly five members: ok, wrong_answer, timeout, unavailable, error.

claims.text: A probe either measures whether the lane is ALIVE and the bytes arrived, or whether the lane's reasoning is the right SHAPE. Only liveness trips the exit code -- see the module docstring.
claims.why: SEVERITIES is a closed tuple ('liveness', 'quality'); the exit-code claim is uncheckable but the tuple itself matches the claim.

claims.text: Statuses that mean 'we asked and it did not work'. unavailable is deliberately absent: we never asked, so there is nothing to have failed.
claims.why: FAILING_STATUSES is frozenset({'wrong_answer', 'timeout', 'error'}) and does not include 'unavailable'.

claims.text: Dumb, append-only, no database.
claims.why: DEFAULT_HISTORY_PATH is a simple Path to a .jsonl file; no database machinery is present.

claims.text: Cheapest sensible local model. This runs often; the 32b is not a health check, it is a bill.
claims.why: DEFAULT_OLLAMA_MODEL is 'qwen2.5-coder:7b', a 7b model.

claims.text: Vendor keys, spelled the way the operator types them (same set as council.session.VENDOR_KEYS so --vendors means one thing repo-wide).
claims.why: This chunk defines VENDOR_KEYS as ('anthropic', 'openai', 'google', 'local') but cannot compare with council.session.VENDOR_KEYS because that module is not visible.

claims.text: How much of a reply is kept on the record. Enough to see what a lane actually said, not enough to turn history.jsonl into a transcript store.
claims.why: REPLY_TRIM is a constant 400; the record-keeping behaviour is not in this chunk but the constant matches the stated purpose.

claims.text: Trailing window for the median comparison. Long enough to be a baseline, short enough that a lane which legitimately got faster stops being compared against last month.
claims.why: TRAILING_WINDOW is 20, a plausible window; the comparison logic is elsewhere but the constant exists.

claims.text: A lane counts as materially slower only if it is BOTH a large multiple of its median AND absolutely slow enough for a human to care. Either test alone cries wolf: a 0.2s -> 0.6s local hop is 3x and means nothing.
claims.where: comment above SLOWER_RATIO and SLOWER_ABS_S, lines 153-156
claims.why: Two constants are defined: SLOWER_RATIO = 2.0 and SLOWER_ABS_S = 2.0, matching the 'both' condition.

claims.text: A fresh probe nonce, e.g. K7F3A9C1. Fresh PER PROBE PER LANE, not per run: a reused nonce cannot distinguish a lane that answered from a lane (or a cache, or a shared transcript) that echoed somebody else's answer -- which is the exact confusion the anchoring incident was made of.
claims.why: new_nonce returns 'K' + secrets.token_hex(4).upper()[:7], which is fresh per call; the per-probe-per-lane usage is a caller contract not visible here, but the function itself produces a fresh nonce.

claims.text: Deterministic per-nonce randomness, so build and check agree. The prompt varies every run (a probe a model has memorised measures nothing) while the checker still knows the right answer without carrying state between the two halves of a probe.
claims.why: _rng seeds random.Random with f'dcanary:{nonce}', which is deterministic for a given nonce.

claims.text: Disjoint from _FILLER_WORDS on purpose: the arrival tail token must not be findable anywhere in the padding, or a reply could satisfy the tail check by quoting the middle of the prompt.
claims.why: Comparing _FILLER_WORDS and _TAIL_WORDS, no word appears in both sets (verified: lantern/meadow/cobble... vs harbor/beacon/trellis...).

claims.text: Invented one-line summaries. None of these describes a real file in this repo, and none of them may contain 'roll'/'revert' -- the comprehension
claims.where: comment above _SUMMARIES, line 198 (truncated at chunk end)
claims.why: The _SUMMARIES constant and the rest of the comment are cut off by the chunk boundary; no summaries are present to verify.

observations.what: DEFAULT_HISTORY_PATH is a relative path (runs/canary/history.jsonl), so the 'append-only' history location depends on the current working directory; a canary run from a different directory would write to a different file, silently fragmenting the baseline.
The comment for VENDOR_KEYS claims it matches council.session.VENDOR_KEYS, but that module is not visible in this chunk; divergence would break the 'one meaning repo-wide' claim.

new_nonce uses secrets.token_hex(4).upper()[:7] after a 'K' prefix; the regex _NONCE_RE expects 8 uppercase alphanumerics after 'NONCE-', which matches the 8-character nonce (K + 7 hex), so the regex and generator align.
